skill.name: gcp-cloud-run
skill.description: Build production-ready serverless applications on Google Cloud Run, including container services, Cloud Run Functions, cold start tuning, Pub/Sub, Cloud SQL, and secrets.
skill.summary: Guides Cloud Run service, function, scaling, networking, database, and secret patterns for production serverless applications.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: AI review found that the static alerts are false positives from a single Markdown documentation skill. The flagged content consists of Cloud Run examples, placeholders, environment variable patterns, Secret Manager usage, and code fences. No prompt injection, malicious execution path, credential exfiltration, or unauthorized network behavior was found.

static_findings.snippet: Message: Global mutable state may cause issues with concurrent requests.

- user needs AWS serverless -> aws-serverless (Lambda, API Gateway, SAM)

content.value_statement: Cloud Run projects need correct deployment, scaling, networking, and secret patterns. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical templates for production-ready GCP serverless work.
actual_capabilities: Provides Cloud Run service patterns with Dockerfile, Cloud Build, and gcloud deployment examples.
Explains Cloud Run Functions for HTTP, Pub/Sub, and Cloud Storage event handling.
Guides cold start tuning with startup CPU boost, minimum instances, image size, and lazy initialization.
Shows Pub/Sub integration patterns for push subscriptions, publishers, and dead letter queues.
Covers Cloud SQL, Secret Manager, VPC connector, timeout, and concurrency considerations.
Lists validation checks for credentials, root containers, ports, temp files, and synchronous file operations.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a live deployment engine.
Users must adapt regions, project names, IAM, and resource limits to their own environment.
It does not replace security review, load testing, or cost analysis for production systems.
Some examples use placeholders and must not be copied without configuration changes.

use_cases.title: Launch a Cloud Run API
use_cases.description: Create a containerized web service with deployment, health checks, scaling, and runtime configuration guidance.

use_cases.title: Design Event-Driven Processing
use_cases.description: Plan Pub/Sub, Cloud Storage, and Cloud Run Functions patterns for asynchronous workloads.

use_cases.title: Improve Production Reliability
use_cases.description: Review cold starts, concurrency, timeouts, VPC behavior, database connections, and secret handling.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Service
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new Cloud Run service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GCP Cloud Run skill to design a basic Cloud Run service for my API. Include deployment settings and required files.

prompt_templates.title: Add Event Processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GCP Cloud Run skill to add Pub/Sub event processing to my service. Include retry, acknowledgement, and dead letter guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Production Scaling
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for performance and cost tuning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GCP Cloud Run skill to review my Cloud Run scaling plan. Recommend concurrency, CPU, memory, min instances, and timeout settings.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Deployment Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a production readiness review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GCP Cloud Run skill to review this deployment architecture for security, reliability, networking, database access, and secrets.

output_examples.input: I need a Cloud Run service for a Node.js API.
output: A service layout with Dockerfile, application entry point, health endpoint, and Cloud Build deployment flow.
Recommended Cloud Run settings for memory, CPU, min instances, max instances, and concurrency.
Notes about non-root containers, the PORT environment variable, and graceful shutdown.

output_examples.input: My Cloud Run service has slow cold starts.
output: A cold start review covering image size, startup CPU boost, lazy loading, memory, and minimum instances.
A prioritized action list for latency-sensitive services.

output_examples.input: I need Pub/Sub processing with Cloud Run.
output: A push subscription design with message validation, retry behavior, and acknowledgement handling.
Guidance for publishing messages and configuring a dead letter queue.

best_practices: Replace every placeholder project, region, service, and resource name before deployment.
Use Secret Manager or workload identity for secrets and credentials.
Validate concurrency, timeout, CPU, memory, and networking settings under realistic load.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode service account keys, API keys, or database passwords in source code.
Do not deploy public unauthenticated services unless that access is explicitly required.
Do not write large temporary files to /tmp without accounting for memory usage.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that a user must review and run separately.

faq.question: Can it help with Cloud Run Functions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes HTTP, Pub/Sub, and Cloud Storage event patterns for second generation functions.

faq.question: Does it cover cold start optimization?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers startup CPU boost, minimum instances, lazy initialization, image size, memory, and CPU settings.

faq.question: Does it explain secret handling?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends Secret Manager, environment-mounted secrets, file-mounted secrets, and API access patterns.

faq.question: Is it specific to one programming language?
faq.answer: No. It includes Node.js, Python, Dockerfile, YAML, and gcloud examples.

faq.question: What should users verify before production use?
faq.answer: Users should verify IAM, public access, networking, timeouts, scaling, cost, and security controls.
